study: What does the GPU-FEM solve cost when CG is allowed to converge?
why: Table 20's timings at N>=401 are the cost of a TRUNCATED solve: CG hit its 2000-iteration cap on every Newton step and never converged. Section 8.5 predicted the converged cost from two separately measured pieces. This tests that prediction instead of leaving it a model.
the_prediction_was_fixed_before_the_run: the cell printed 'CG should converge in about 5.011 x N iterations per Newton solve' for both resolutions BEFORE launching, so it could not be adjusted afterwards to fit.
settings: identical to the point-8 sweep in every respect except cg_max_iter, raised from 2000 to 8000. B1 x Neo-Hookean, Q4, 10 load steps, newton_max 30, newton_tol 1e-7, cg_tol 1e-6, FP64, A100-SXM4-80GB, checkpoint_dir set (as the original sweep also did, so the wall clocks are comparable).

WHAT_IT_CONFIRMS.1_the_O_N_CG_law: CG converged in 2,520.8 and 3,528.1 iterations per Newton solve against the 2,511 and 3,513 predicted from the three converged rows of the original sweep -- 0.4% at both. The 5.011 x N law was fitted on N=101, 201 and 301 and holds at N=701, seven times the largest mesh it was fitted on.
WHAT_IT_CONFIRMS.2_CG_converged_everywhere: cg_failures is 0 at both resolutions, so 8000 was a sufficient budget and these are genuinely converged solves -- the first this solver has produced at these sizes.
WHAT_IT_CONFIRMS.3_Newton_drops_when_CG_converges: at N=701 the Newton count fell from 30 to 20, exactly the 2 per load step that every converged row of the original sweep showed. This was predicted in advance: a truncated CG returns an inexact direction and costs extra Newton steps. At N=501 it was already 20 and stayed 20.
WHAT_IT_CONFIRMS.4_the_per_iteration_cost_model: cost per CG iteration is 40.9 ms at N=501 and 74.9 ms at N=701, against 40.4 and 74.8 in the truncated runs -- 1.3% and 0.2% apart. Two independent runs, one truncated and one converged, agree on the matvec cost, which is what the O(DOF) claim rests on.

THE_DIRECTION_IS_NOW_SETTLED.what_the_report_said: section 8.5 in v36 says the direction of the error in Table 20 'is not one-signed: allowing CG to converge would add iterations to each Newton step while removing Newton steps, and this study does not establish which effect is larger.'
THE_DIRECTION_IS_NOW_SETTLED.now_it_does: Table 20 UNDERSTATES the converged cost at both measured sizes. N=501: 1,616 s -> 2,064 s, +28%. N=701: 4,487 s -> 5,286 s, +18%. In us/DOF: 3,219 -> 4,109 and 4,566 -> 5,379.
THE_DIRECTION_IS_NOW_SETTLED.why_the_gap_narrows_with_size: the added iterations and the removed Newton steps partly cancel, and how much depends on how badly the truncated run was over-iterating in Newton. At N=501 Newton was already minimal so there was nothing to recover and the full +28% shows; at N=701 dropping 30 Newton steps to 20 claws most of it back.

EXTRAPOLATED_NOT_MEASURED.caveat: N=1001 and N=1401 were NOT re-run -- 4 h and 11.6 h respectively. These use the now twice-confirmed model (20 Newton steps x 5.011 x N CG iterations x the measured per-iteration cost) and are predictions, to be labelled as such wherever they appear.

N1401.note: only +5% because the truncated run burned 67 Newton steps against the 20 a converged CG needs, so almost all the extra CG work is paid for by the Newton steps it removes.

memory_unaffected: peak 1,122 MB at N=501 and 1,567 MB at N=701, against 1,123 and 1,568 in the truncated runs. Memory does not depend on iteration count, as section 8.5 already states.
cost: 2 h 2 m 50 s total on an A100.
provenance: transcribed from the Colab stdout of Round6_CG_Convergence_Check on 2026-08-29; the run's own JSON is at pfem_run/gpu_fem_cg_check/ on Drive.

A_TRANSCRIPTION_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.what: checked against the run's own JSON on Drive and two numbers were wrong in this file.
A_TRANSCRIPTION_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.solve_s_at_N501: was 2064.0, is 2062.659. The us_per_dof beside it was already right (4108.87 = 2062.659/502002), so the two fields in this file contradicted each other and the wall clock was the wrong one.
A_TRANSCRIPTION_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.ms_per_cg_iter: was 40.94 and 74.91, which is solve_s divided by CG iterations, not CG time divided by CG iterations. Both forms are now stored and named. The CG-time form is 40.82 and 74.83.
A_TRANSCRIPTION_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.does_any_conclusion_change: no. +28% and +18% against Table 20 are unchanged (2062.659/1616.061 = 1.276), the us/DOF figures were already correct, and the truncated-vs-converged agreement is 1.3% and 0.2% on the solve_s form, which is the only form the truncated sweep supports.
A_TRANSCRIPTION_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.why_the_solve_s_form_is_the_one_quoted: the point-8 sweep recorded no t_cg_s at N=501 or N=701, so a like-for-like comparison has to divide solve time on both sides. CG is 99.8% of the solve here, which bounds what that substitution can hide.
